Required coverage and evidence: The required CS core provides 61 credits of fundamental and advanced computing. CS 250 and CS 370 assess software construction, tools and testing; CS 451 adds reliable data pipelines and CS 455 automated deployment, monitoring and recovery. CS 402 covers security and privacy. ISLM 101, CS 340 and CS 411 assess ethics and societal impacts. Required coverage and assessment do not depend on elective choices.

The required CS core provides 61 credits, including three in Research Methods in Computing. It provides 58 computing credits without research methods, capstones, co-op or electives. CS 103 remains within the separate mathematics/statistics allocation.

Curriculum requirement: Depth in algorithms, theory, language concepts, and software development
Required coverage and evidence: CS 201 and CS 220 assess data structures, algorithm correctness, and complexity. CS 330 assesses formal computation and reductions. CS 320 covers language semantics and paradigms through an interpreter project. CS 101, CS 102, and CS 250 assess software construction, testing, and team development. CS 370 adds an integrated web and mobile application project.

CS 101 and CS 102 provide seven credits of sustained Python practice. Students design and test modular and object-oriented programs in supervised labs and applied assessments. CS 240 adds systems programming in C.

Curriculum requirement: Exposure to the required systems topics
Required coverage and evidence: CS 210 covers architecture and organization, CS 230 covers information management, CS 260 covers networking and communication, CS 310 covers operating systems, and CS 401 covers parallel and distributed computing.

Curriculum requirement: Computing systems at multiple abstraction levels
Required coverage and evidence: Students progress from digital circuits, processor construction and instruction execution in CS 210 to system calls and resource management in CS 240 and CS 310, then to network protocols in CS 260 and distributed services in CS 401. Lab work connects choices at each level to program behavior. CS 370 connects application interfaces and APIs to shared backend services. CS 451 and CS 455 connect data pipelines, containers, infrastructure and operational services to these abstraction levels.

CS 410 and CS 411 form a six-credit project. The design review identifies techniques from earlier courses. The final assessment uses a working solution, integration tests, evaluation results, and an individual defense to show how students applied those techniques.

The plan requires 20 credits. MATH 101 (4), CS 103 (3), MATH 120 (3), STAT 220 (4), MATH 230 (3), and MATH 340 (3) cover discrete mathematics, probability, statistics, linear algebra, calculus, optimization, and numerical analysis. CS 103 Discrete Structures remains a mathematics course for this allocation and is excluded from the 61-credit CS core total.
PHYS 101, PHYS 102, and BIO 101 provide 10 credits of non-computing laboratory science. Students formulate hypotheses, control variables, analyze measurements and uncertainty, and report conclusions.
